title: Existence and universal property of strict logarithmic pullbacks
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $h:Y'\to Y$ be morphisms of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], with $h$ strict [def-per-strict-log-morphism]. Use the arbitrary log morphisms of [def-trf-log-ideal-chart-presentation] and their composites [lem-sfb-log-morphism-operations]. If the scheme map of $f$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], there is an fs locally Noetherian $X'$ with $p:X'\to X$, $q:X'\to Y'$ and a common log composite, where $p$ is strict and the underlying square is a scheme pullback. For every such representative, compatible log maps $a:T\to X$ and $b:T\to Y'$ from any log structure on any scheme $T$ factor uniquely as a log map to $X'$. Compatibility and factorization include equality of all log-section maps; no fineness, saturation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $T$.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69; VIII 3.3.5--3.3.6, p.107. The direct strict-product construction in parent proof step 3, written by F3.

proof.text: Take the scheme product and give it the log structure associated to the inverse image of the log structure on X. Locally an fs chart Q on X pulls back to the same chart Q on the product. Associated chart maps are given on pairs by [z,u] mapping to the prescribed image of z times u. The unit-pushout relations hold because log maps preserve the structural map and units. The formulas agree on overlaps and glue. Strictness of h gives the other projection as a log map and the common composite.

The second projection is locally of finite presentation by base change of the underlying f. In particular it is locally of finite type and its source is locally Noetherian over the locally Noetherian Yprime. Its charts Q are fs, so the constructed object is in the required category.

For compatible maps from any test log structure, the scheme product supplies the unique underlying map. On associated chart pairs use [z,u] mapping to a(z)u. The relations make this a log map, and chart elements and units generate, proving uniqueness. For any other representative, strictness of p identifies its log structure with this associated inverse image by the canonical stalk map; use the same formula. Normalization on relative pointed sections fixes the resulting log maps, rather than merely their abstract stalk isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem strictLogPullback_universal {X Y Y' : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}}
    (f : EtaleLogHom X Y) (h : EtaleLogHom Y' Y) (hh : h.IsStrict) :
    (LocallyOfFinitePresentation f.base →
      ∃ (X' : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (p : EtaleLogHom X' X)
        (q : EtaleLogHom X' Y') (c : EtaleLogHom X' Y),
        p.IsStrict ∧ IsPullback p.base q.base f.base h.base ∧
          p.CompEq f c ∧ q.CompEq h c) ∧
    (∀ (X' : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (p : EtaleLogHom X' X)
      (q : EtaleLogHom X' Y') (c : EtaleLogHom X' Y),
      p.IsStrict → IsPullback p.base q.base f.base h.base →
        p.CompEq f c → q.CompEq h c →
          p.toLogMap.IsLogPullback q.toLogMap f.toLogMap h.toLogMap)
